source_text: quod post resurrectionem tales processus futuros esse dicamus, ut ibi incipiant homines quae hic noluerint Dei mandata complere
pass_a_gloss: that we say after the resurrection there will be such advances, that there human beings begin to fulfill the commandments of God which they were unwilling to fulfill here
pass_b_english: They say that after the resurrection there will be such progress that people will begin there to fulfill the commandments of God that they were unwilling to fulfill here.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
